#  [search]: when rows appear
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# "fi" to find Firefox isn't cluttered. @name and !level tokens don't count.
min_chars = 5

# The most rows to show. GNOME displays about five per category.
max_rows = 5


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  [prompt]: the prompt box (spotlight-style window)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Open it from the app grid ("Agent Search"), with the keyboard shortcut chosen
#  at install time (./install.sh --shortcut '<Primary><Super>space'), by clicking
#  the Agent Search icon in search results, or with:  llm-search prompt [text]
#  It shows the same rows as the search bar. Enter sends, Up/Down choose, Esc closes.

idle_minutes = 30

#  [[app]]: app agents

#  link (url) or runs a program (command).
#
#  KEYS
#    id          Required. Unique, lowercase. Also matches @id in the search bar.
#    name        Required. The row's title.
#    url         A link to open, e.g. claude://... or https://...

#    cwd         Folder the command runs in. Default "~" (your home folder).
#    requires    Programs that must be installed, e.g. ["claude"]. If any is
#                missing, the row is hidden instead of failing.
#    icon        An icon name from your icon theme, e.g. "utilities-terminal".
#    tags        What this agent is good at. Used for ranking (see [routing]).
#                Built-in rules use: coding, writing, reasoning, private, fast.
#    models      Models the agent accepts through {model}. Lets @opus etc. pick one.
#    efforts     Effort levels it accepts through {effort}: low medium high xhigh max.
#    priority    A number added to its score. Higher means it ranks higher. Default 0.

#                receive it), so you can paste it with Ctrl+V.

#                (Also a switch on the settings window's Agents page.)

#    {model}     the model picked with @name, or empty
#    {effort}    the effort from !level (or the suggested one), or empty

#    dropped, so  ?q={prompt}&model={model}  becomes  ?q=hello  when no model is chosen.

#    the prompt is always passed as one argument, so quotes, ; and $ in it are safe.

id = "claude-chat"
name = "Ask Claude"
url = "claude://claude.ai/new?q={prompt}"
icon = "claude-desktop"
tags = ["writing", "reasoning", "general"]
priority = 1.0        # the default choice for everyday questions

#   url = "claude://code/new?q={prompt}&folder=/home/you/Projects/my-app"

id = "claude-code"
name = "Claude Code"
url = "claude://code/new?q={prompt}"
icon = "claude-desktop"
tags = ["coding", "agent"]

# and effort you choose (@opus !high). Needs the Claude Code CLI:
#   curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash   then run `claude` once to log in.

name = "Claude Code (terminal)"

icon = "utilities-terminal"
tags = ["coding", "agent"]
models = ["opus", "sonnet", "haiku", "fable"]
efforts = ["low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max"]
priority = 0.5        # ranks above the desktop "Claude Code" row for coding prompts

high_effort_patterns = [

tag = "coding"
weight = 3
patterns = [

tag = "writing"
weight = 2
patterns = ['\b(write|draft|email|rewrite|summari[sz]e|proofread|tone|essay|letter|post)\b']

tag = "reasoning"
weight = 2
patterns = ['\b(why|explain|compare|plan|decide|pros and cons|trade-?offs?)\b']

tag = "private"
weight = 4
patterns = ['\b(private|confidential|offline|local only|password|medical|salary)\b']

tag = "fast"
weight = 1
patterns = ['^\S+(\s+\S+){0,5}\??$']   # very short questions (up to about six words)

#   url = "claude://code/new?q={prompt}&folder=/home/you/Projects/my-app"
[[app]]
id = "claude-code"
name = "Claude Code"
url = "claude://code/new?q={prompt}"
icon = "claude-desktop"
tags = ["coding", "agent"]

# Claude Code in a terminal window. Runs the prompt IMMEDIATELY, with the model
# and effort you choose (@opus !high). Needs the Claude Code CLI:
#   curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash   then run `claude` once to log in.
# Hidden until `claude` is installed.
[[app]]
id = "claude-cli"
enabled = false
name = "Claude Code (terminal)"
command = ["ptyxis", "--new-window", "--", "claude",
           ["--model", "{model}"], ["--effort", "{effort}"], "--", "{prompt}"]
cwd = "~/Projects"             # tip: set this to the folder you usually work in, e.g. "~/Projects"
requires = ["ptyxis", "claude"]
icon = "utilities-terminal"
tags = ["coding", "agent"]
models = ["opus", "sonnet", "haiku", "fable"]
efforts = ["low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max"]
priority = 0.5        # ranks above the desktop "Claude Code" row for coding prompts

#  Setup guide: docs/PROVIDERS.md. Leave this commented out until the proxy runs.

# auto_model = "smart-router"


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  [routing]: how rows are ranked, and which effort is suggested
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  HOW RANKING WORKS
#    1. Each [[routing.rule]] below checks your prompt against its patterns.
#    2. If any pattern matches, every agent whose `tags` include the rule's `tag`
#       gets the rule's `weight` added to its score.
#    3. Each agent's `priority` is added too, and rows are shown highest first.
#    An @name always comes first, and the best app agent always stays visible.
#
#    Worked example: "fix this python traceback"
#      The coding rule matches (python, traceback)  → +3 for agents tagged "coding"
#      Claude Code (terminal) = 3 + 0.5 priority = 3.5   ← first
#      Claude Code            = 3 + 0           = 3.0
#      Ask Claude             = 0 + 1.0         = 1.0
#
#  SUGGESTED EFFORT (when you don't type !level)
#    high    if any high_effort_patterns entry matches
#    low     if the prompt has low_effort_max_words words or fewer
#    medium  otherwise (high for prompts over 60 words)
#    Agents that don't support the suggested level use the closest one they do.
#
#  PATTERNS are regular expressions, matched case-insensitively anywhere in the
#  prompt. Write them in 'single quotes' so backslashes stay literal:
#    '\bgit\b'       the word "git" (\b = word boundary), but not "digit"
#    'deploy|ship'   either word
#    '```'           a fenced code block
#  Try patterns at https://regex101.com (choose the Python flavor).
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
[routing]
low_effort_max_words = 8
high_effort_patterns = [
  '\b(why|design|architect\w*|debug\w*|compare|trade-?offs?|plan|prove|step by step|analy[sz]e)\b',
]

# Each [[routing.rule]] block is one rule: tag, weight, and a list of patterns.
[[routing.rule]]
tag = "coding"
weight = 3
patterns = [
  '\b(code|function|class|bug|regex|script|refactor|compile|stack ?trace|traceback|exception|git|bash|python|javascript|typescript|rust|golang|sql|api|unit tests?)\b',
  '```',          # a pasted code block
  '\w+\(\)',      # something that looks like a call: main()
]

[[routing.rule]]
tag = "writing"
weight = 2
patterns = ['\b(write|draft|email|rewrite|summari[sz]e|proofread|tone|essay|letter|post)\b']

[[routing.rule]]
tag = "reasoning"
weight = 2
patterns = ['\b(why|explain|compare|plan|decide|pros and cons|trade-?offs?)\b']

# Sends sensitive prompts towards agents tagged "private" (e.g. local models).
[[routing.rule]]
tag = "private"
weight = 4
patterns = ['\b(private|confidential|offline|local only|password|medical|salary)\b']

[[routing.rule]]
tag = "fast"
weight = 1
patterns = ['^\S+(\s+\S+){0,5}\??$']   # very short questions (up to about six words)

# ==============================================================================

# ==============================================================================

#    The installer copies this file there once and never overwrites your copy.
#    The original is examples/config/agents.toml in the project repo.
#
#  APPLYING CHANGES
#    Saved changes apply on the next search, or the next time the prompt box opens.
#
#  THE SETTINGS WINDOW
#    The gear on the prompt box (or Ctrl+,) edits this same file: it changes just the
#    value on the line in question and keeps every comment, so this file and the
#    window always agree. "Restore Defaults" there resets the limits in [search],
#    [prompt] and [routing] to factory values, keeping your agents and rules.
#
#  TESTING CHANGES WITHOUT GNOME
#    llm-search query fix this python traceback   # the rows GNOME would get, top first
#    llm-search test                              # the project's own tests
#    If the file has a syntax error, no Agent Search rows appear at all; check with
#        python3 -c "import tomllib; tomllib.load(open('$HOME/.llm-search/config/agents.toml','rb'))"
#
#  TOML IN 30 SECONDS
#    # comment                     Anything after # is ignored.
#    key = "text"                  Strings use double quotes; \ starts an escape (\n, \").
#    key = 'C:\raw\text'           Single quotes are literal: no escapes. Use them for regexes.

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  [search]: when rows appear
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Prompts shorter than this many characters show no Agent Search rows, so typing
# "fi" to find Firefox isn't cluttered. @name and !level tokens don't count.
min_chars = 3

# The most rows to show. GNOME displays about five per category.
max_rows = 5


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  [prompt]: the prompt box (spotlight-style window)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Open it from the app grid ("Agent Search"), with the keyboard shortcut chosen
#  at install time (./install.sh --shortcut '<Primary><Super>space'), by clicking
#  the Agent Search icon in search results, or with:  llm-search prompt [text]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  [[app]]: app agents
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Each [[app]] block is one row that can appear in search. A row either opens a
#  link (url) or runs a program (command).
#
#  KEYS
#    id          Required. Unique, lowercase. Also matches @id in the search bar.
#    name        Required. The row's title.
#    url         A link to open, e.g. claude://... or https://...
#    command     A program to run, as a list of arguments (see "COMMANDS" below).
#    cwd         Folder the command runs in. Default "~" (your home folder).

#    models      Models the agent accepts through {model}. Lets @opus etc. pick one.
#    efforts     Effort levels it accepts through {effort}: low medium high xhigh max.
#    priority    A number added to its score. Higher means it ranks higher. Default 0.
#    copy_prompt true also copies the prompt to the clipboard (for apps that can't
#                receive it), so you can paste it with Ctrl+V.
#    enabled     false hides the row without deleting it. Default true.

#    {prompt}    what you typed, minus @name and !level

#    Values are URL-encoded for you. Query parameters that end up empty are
#    dropped, so  ?q={prompt}&model={model}  becomes  ?q=hello  when no model is chosen.

#  COMMANDS
#    Written as a list, one item per argument, and never run through a shell:
#    the prompt is always passed as one argument, so quotes, ; and $ in it are safe.
#      - An item whose placeholder is empty is left out.
#      - A nested list is an optional group, left out as a whole if any of its
